Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we want to kick off contracting for the initial integration (Order Form for 2 dedicated instances + standard support). I attached the SOW and your security questionnaire.

High-level asks from our side to get contracting moving:
- Confirm the primary billing and legal contacts for Parkside (name, email, company entity).
- Which entity should be on the MSA? You mentioned Parkside Labs, Inc. — please confirm full legal name and jurisdiction.
- Any deviations from our standard MSA you expect (data residency, IP, export controls)? Call those out now so Legal can triage.
- Desired signer path (executive vs. procurement vs. legal) and estimated timeline for signatures.

I've looped in Kimberly from Sales Ops to collect party data and Marissa from our Contracting team who will own redlines.

Attachments:
- Parkside_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW; scope + pricing)
- Parkside_Security_Form.xlsx (security questionnaire — please fill sections highlighted in yellow)

Next step: If you can reply with party/legal contact and any specific clause items by EOD Thursday (8/12), Marissa will start a first-pass redline and return a tracked MSA.

Thanks —

Hi Rohan —

Thanks — attaching a quick party sheet here (see inline). Confirming: legal entity is Parkside Labs, Inc., incorporated in Delaware. Primary billing contact is me (asha.patel@parksidelabs.com). Procurement is handled by our vendor ops team (vendor.ops@parksidelabs.com).

Two items to flag up front:
1) Data residency: we need EU-only residency for EU customer data (we have a handful of EU customers in scope). Is that supported under the Dedicated offering?
2) Liability cap: our counsel will request the cap be tied to fees for the first 12 months, rather than a fixed dollar amount.

Our legal team (copied) will fill the security form and flag any redlines. We typically run contracts through VP Legal (Stella Marino) for signature. Timeline: aim for 2-3 weeks depending on redlines.

Thanks —

Thanks Asha / Rohan —

I've reviewed the party sheet and the security form (preliminary). Quick intake notes and what we'll do next:

Intake observations:
- Entity confirmed: Parkside Labs, Inc. (DE).
- EU data residency request: this is feasible but may require a data residency exhibit + operational notes. I'll add Exhibit D (Data Residency) to the MSA and propose language for region-scoped processing.
- Liability cap ask: I'll flag with Legal team — typical counter we see is equal to the last 12 months' fees or a multiple; we'll propose a fee-tied cap and include fallback language if counsel pushes for a higher limit.

Action plan (next 48 hours):
1) I'll produce a tracked MSA (Redwood_MSA_Template_v3.docx) with: exhibit placeholder for Data Residency; clause alternatives for liability; and a standard vendor security appendix filled with references to the completed Parkside_Security_Form.xlsx.
2) Rohan / Kimberly: please confirm the signer path (VP Legal -> CEO) vs Procurement -> CEO. Asha indicated VP Legal (Stella Marino) — is procurement still required to countersign? We ask for a canonical signer map so we can populate the signature block and speed routing.
3) If Parkside needs the MSA redlines in DocuSign-friendly .docx, I will attach that for easier comment.

Attachments to expect in my next email: Redwood_MSA_Template_v3.docx (tracked), redline summary (1-pager).

If there are any regulatory constraints (e.g., data localization law citations or local EU subsidiary entity requirements), please add in your reply so we can surface to Legal.

Thanks —
